lines:
Phase 2 of 3 of the workflow-revision rebinding design (aworkit.trusted_core.revision_rebind). Phase 1 makes a Chat able to adopt a newer workflow revision between turns; this phase makes the resulting chain honest in everything the user can see, export or fork.

Deliverables.
- Revision-aware evidence: Run details, the Model context panel and the event projections show which revision each turn, node span and context revision belongs to, without relabelling anything already committed. One lineage, stamped — graphRevision (adopted workflow revision) and contextRevision (context lineage entry) stay distinct names, and no view may present them as the same thing.
- Portable history and fork: a Chat that adopted revisions carries its revision chain through export and import, and forking starts the child under an explicitly named revision rather than an implicit "latest". A portable branch must remain interpretable on another machine where the saved workflow may have moved on.
- Grants and approvals reconciliation: filesystem grants and saved tool approvals recorded for the Chat are reconciled with the adopted selection. A grant whose tool binding the adopted revision no longer selects is reported and either retained explicitly or dropped with a note; authority the adopted revision adds still requires the phase-1 consent step and is never inherited from the earlier revision's consent.
- Unreplayable-round preview, end to end: the pre-adoption report names the exact recorded tool rounds the candidate cannot replay (count, capability, turn), and the post-adoption path is verified to omit them from the outgoing request, record the decline, continue the turn, and re-import what is representable on the next turn.
- Documentation: the desktop notification/run-details surface explains a shorter-memory turn caused by an adoption, so a weaker answer after a rebind is traceable rather than mysterious.

Non-goals. Research mode (phase 3); automatic or silent adoption; retroactive relabelling of committed turns or context revisions; rewriting recorded tool calls; extending a deadline.

Tests. Revision labels in every projection; portable export/import round-trip of a rebonded Chat; fork inheritance of the chain and its explicit revision; grants reconciliation with and without consent; the unreplayable-round preview matching what the admission check actually declines; and a decline-then-recover cycle spanning an adoption boundary.

Depends on. Phase 1 (task 123) and the region-aware validator and loop-frame predicate from task 116.

data.title: Revision-aware evidence, export and grant reconciliation (phase 2 of 3)
